subject: general
question: The lengths of the diagonals of a rhombus compare as 3 times some value to 4 times that same value. If the area of the rhombus is 216 cm², what are the actual lengths of the two diagonals?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of diagonals d₁ : d₂ = 3 : 4

Area = 1/2 × (Product of ratio parts) × x²

216 = 1/2 × 3 × 4 × x² ⇒ 216 = 6x²

x² = 36 ⇒ x = 6

Actual diagonals = 3 × 6 and 4 × 6 = 18 cm and 24 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 18 cm and 24 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio of diagonals = 3 : 4, Area of rhombus = 216 cm².

**Formula Used:** Area of Rhombus = 1/2 × d₁ × d₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5d4185ae34bb1acf87843d553473cb5a4cf84a4b323fe6fbc295b60d0f3dd864.png] 

⇒ Let the lengths of the diagonals be 3x and 4x.

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 3x × 4x

⇒ 216 = 6x²

⇒ x² = 216 ÷ 6

⇒ x² = 36

⇒ x = √36 = 6

⇒ First diagonal (d₁) = 3 × 6 = 18 cm

⇒ Second diagonal (d₂) = 4 × 6 = 24 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 18 cm and 24 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Rhombus

A rhombus is a quadrilateral with all four sides equal. Opposite angles are equal and adjacent angles are supplementary (sum to 180°).

Diagonal Property

The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles (90°).

Side-Diagonal Relation

If side is 'a' and diagonals are d₁ and d₂, then 4a² = d₁² + d₂².

Perimeter of Rhombus

The perimeter is calculated as 4 × side.</p
